description:
FOUND s438d (Opus 5) by the #454 probe set, and PRE-EXISTING: identical on a
373fd5d worktree, so #454's narrowing neither caused nor widened it.

  use feature "signatures";
  my $y = 5;
  sub f ($x = $y) { "f($x)" }
  print f(), "\n";            # perl: f(5)      PCL: f()

WHY IT IS SILENT: a signature DEFAULT is an expression evaluated inside the
sub, so `$y` there is a genuine capture of the file lexical -- exactly the
thing `_check_sub_captures` exists to refuse.  But that gate asks
`_block_captures_name($child->block, â¦)`, and the default is in the SIGNATURE,
which is a sibling of the block, not part of it.  So the capture is never seen:
no refusal, no promotion, and the default reads an unbound name as undef.

#454 made the ADJACENT question right (a signature PARAMETER shadows a
same-named file lexical, so it is not a capture) and deliberately did NOT
touch this one: `_signature_param_canons` returns only the LEADING symbol of
each top-level comma-separated part, so `$y` is not treated as declared.  That
is the correct half; the missing half is that nobody looks INSIDE the default.

FIX SHAPE: the capture gate should scan the sub's signature defaults as well as
its block.  The cheapest correct form is to ask `_block_captures_name` about
the signature node too (it takes a PPI node and does its own shadow analysis) â
but the shadow rules differ: inside a default, EARLIER parameters are in scope
(`sub f ($a, $b = $a)` is legal and $a is the parameter), so a default's uses
must be checked against the parameters to its LEFT before being called a
capture.  `_signature_param_canons` already computes that list in order.

WHETHER TO REFUSE OR TO PROMOTE is the second decision: a refusal is the honest
minimum and matches every other capture, but the file lexical could equally be
promoted like any other captured one (the machinery exists) and then the
default would simply work.  Measure which shapes occur before choosing --
this one occurs in ZERO files of the four populations (the #454 A/B: 951 files,
0 DIFF), so a refusal costs nothing measurable today.

BAR: probe rows vs perl for `($x = $y)` (capture), `($a, $b = $a)` (NOT a
capture -- an earlier parameter), `($x = SOME_CONST)` (not a capture); a row in
Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t (#454's guard, which already carries the parameter
half); scoping change â the full sweep is the gate, plus the gate-SET scan over
both populations if a refusal is added.

DONE s443g (Opus, agent G round 4), commit 9c5e983 (orig e3449f7), ff-merged s444.  A sub is its BLOCK and its SIGNATURE: _sub_captures_name is the ONE resolver for the capture gate, the promoter and the nested-sub hoist; a use inside a DEFAULT is shadowed only by parameters STRICTLY LEFT of its own part (probed: own-default reads the outer; later parts never count).  Fable re-probed f($x=$y)/left-shadow/own-default -- all identical to perl.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a signature DEFAULT that reads an outer lexical gets undef -- `my $y = 5; sub f ($x = $y) {â¦}` gives f() where perl gives f(5); the capture detector scans the BLOCK and a default is not in it
